title: Open Waste Burning Monitoring and Response
problem: Uncontrolled waste burning and related particulate exposure
benefits: Faster detection and coordinated prevention at priority sites.
adaptation: Define locally lawful response protocols and accessible alternatives to burning.
source: GreenHope concept synthesis; validate with local experts.

title: Tiered Landfill Methane Screening
problem: Limited visibility of landfill-gas risks and emission hotspots
requiredData: Appropriate ground or airborne methane measurements
benefits: Prioritizes measurement and mitigation resources without overstating remote observations.
risks: Treating thermal anomalies as methane measurements
adaptation: Use qualified practitioners, site safety controls and fit-for-purpose quantification.
source: Illustrative workflow informed by public methane-management practice.

title: Community Sensor Stewardship Network
problem: Exposure blind spots and limited community trust
benefits: Improves spatial awareness and public participation when quality controls are explicit.
adaptation: Set expectations, maintenance ownership and data-quality labels.

title: Evidence-to-Action Clean Air Sprint
problem: Evidence exists but is not translated into accountable action
benefits: Creates a sequenced, owned and measurable city action portfolio.
adaptation: Align with legal mandates, budgets and affected communities.

title: Health-Centered Air Quality Communication
problem: Technical air data is difficult for residents to act on
benefits: Makes risk communication timely, accessible and action-oriented.
adaptation: Use local languages, trusted messengers and non-digital channels.

title: Data-Driven Waste-Site Prioritization
problem: Inspection resources are not targeted to highest environmental risk
adaptation: Review criteria for local law, equity and data gaps.
